item: confirm the ONE still-unimplemented proposal this round mines: verify unimplemented with a tree sweep and quote its text verbatim

proposal.title: Counter-arm liveness check
verbatim_lines_at_cand: 2. **Counter-arm liveness check.** For each frozen counter, list its arms and require one committed input per arm that moves
that arm's tally away from zero. A passing control set did not reveal that round 53's re-key arm could never fire.
proposal.verbatim_joined: Counter-arm liveness check. For each frozen counter, list its arms and require one committed input per arm that moves that arm's tally away from zero. A passing control set did not reveal that round 53's re-key arm could never fire.
proposal.confidence: high (unimplemented), medium-high (that this is the ONE round 58 mines — the L1 report naming it does not exist yet; wave-1's considerthese seat T58W1ScoutCT returned empty output, see identification_basis)

identification_basis: INFERENCE: the L1 names the mined proposal only in the round-58 report (contract.json line 122: 'considerthese mined separately in the report'), which is not written at dispatch time; no committed or uncommitted round-58 file names it. The identification below is the seat's own, grounded in the cited evidence.

Round-57 contract precedent (.ufo/evidence/round-57/contract.json:164) shows the naming format: 'considerthese/2026-10-28.md proposal 3 (cold-read cost forecast at planning time) mined as a lesson + QUALITY criterion + tools/forecast tool if landed'.

Mining order from the round-56 lesson (corpus/lessons/round-56.md:28-33): proposal 1 mined into QUALITY criterion 107 (revision half; quote half declared unmined in the criterion's own scope sentence); 'Proposals 2-5 remain unmined (at most one per round)'. Round 57 then mined proposal 3 (tools/cold-read-forecast.py exists at C0). Remaining from the latest file at C0: proposals 2, 4, 5.

Round 55's considerthese scribe already picked proposal 2 with the same unimplemented verdict (.ufo/waves/round-55/w1/T55W1ScribeConsiderthese.json: 'implemented': false, 'no tool/criterion enumerates a counter's arms and requires a committed input per arm; QUALITY 105 ... only proves non-zero passing arms on a positive control'); round 55 was rejected-harmed and the draft arm-census never landed as a tool or criterion.

Round 58's substance is counter-arm integrity: the decisive wave-1 finding is the bent-runner forgery (.ufo/waves/round-58/w1/T58W1RevengerC2-receipts/, attack.py Attack B) where a claimant-authored registry-check.py produces the counter's executed and mutants arms without executing rows — exactly the failure class the proposal names; Planned (round 59) re-carries R53.1, the original dead-arm defect the proposal cites.

Proposals 4 and 5 are also unimplemented at C0 but do not match anything round 58 does: no assimilation-backlog tracking was built (C3 adopted exactly one merge/tameshi entry; no census of the backlog exists), and the only pointer repair this round is the single routed R53.5 correction (facts.json new_fixes), not a standing sweep.
